purpose: Anidulafungin is used to treat serious fungal infections, including a bloodstream infection called candidemia and infections inside the belly caused by a fungus called Candida. It is a strong antifungal medicine given to adults who need treatment in a hospital or clinical setting.
how_it_works: Anidulafungin works by attacking the outer wall of the fungal cells, kind of like breaking down the fence that protects the fungus. Without that protective wall, the fungal cells fall apart and die. Your own body cells are not harmed because human cells do not have this type of wall.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, low potassium levels in the blood, and headache. Some people may notice flushing, rash, or itching, especially if the medication is given too quickly through the IV.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as your doctor will want to monitor your liver during treatment. Rarely, serious allergic reactions including swelling, difficulty breathing, or a drop in blood pressure can occur during the infusion. Always let your healthcare team know about all medications you are taking to avoid interactions.
typical_dosing: Anidulafungin is given through an IV (a drip into your vein) once a day in a hospital or clinic. The first dose is usually a higher loading dose of 200 mg, followed by 100 mg once daily on the following days. The length of treatment depends on your infection and how well you respond to the medicine.
